standard.description: This standard prescribes the essential quality requirements, sensory physical characteristics, chemical tolerances, toxic metal thresholds, radiological limits, and microbiological safety criteria for water intended for human consumption (drinking water) across India, regardless of its source (municipal supplies, surface water, groundwater, or tankers).

certification.description: Voluntary/Mandatory. While BIS product certification (ISI Mark) is widely pursued by municipal boards, water treatment plants, and tanker operators as a mark of quality assurance, compliance with its chemical, physical, and biological limits is strictly mandatory across India. It is legally enforced by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) under national food safety laws, making IS 10500 compliance non-negotiable for all water utility boards, commercial food business operators, and drinking water packaging systems.
requirements: Specifies two levels of limits for each parameter: a) An 'Acceptable Limit' (formerly desirable limit) which is the target for safe long-term use; and b) A 'Permissible Limit in the Absence of Alternate Source' which is the maximum tolerable limit when no alternative supplies are available.
Limits the acceptable and permissible pH value of drinking water to a range of 6.5 to 8.5 with no relaxation permitted.
TDS limits are capped at an acceptable limit of 500 mg/l, which may be relaxed to a permissible limit of 2000 mg/l only in the absence of any alternative source.
Restricts total hardness (as CaCO3) to 200 mg/l (acceptable) and 600 mg/l (permissible). Chlorides are restricted to 250 mg/l (acceptable) and 1000 mg/l (permissible).

Fluorides are restricted to 1.0 mg/l (acceptable) and 1.5 mg/l (permissible) to prevent skeletal and dental fluorosis. Nitrates (as NO3) are capped strictly at 45 mg/l with no permissible relaxation to prevent methemoglobinemia (blue baby syndrome).
Iron (Fe) is restricted to 0.3 mg/l with no relaxation. Arsenic (As) is limited strictly to 0.01 mg/l to prevent systemic heavy metal poisoning.

E. coli, thermotolerant coliforms, and total coliform bacteria must be completely non-detectable in any 100 ml sample of drinking water. Any positive detection represents immediate sanitary non-compliance.
Mandates that uranium levels in Table 3 (Sl. No. xiii) must be tested and estimated in accordance with IS 3025 (Part 65) or IS 14194 (Part 3) as updated by Amendment No. 4, November 2021.
When water is chlorinated, a minimum residual free chlorine concentration of 0.2 mg/l must be maintained at the consumer delivery end to prevent secondary microbial growth.

Any observed or calculated test or analysis value expressing chemical concentration, physical turbidity, or radiological counts used to determine code compliance must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value must match the standard's specified value.
